title: Heartbeat coalescer tuning experiment diary
content:
Purpose:
This is a working diary capturing a set of small, targeted experiments that test a lightweight periodic flush mechanism ("heartbeat coalescer") added to the continuous batching loop. Goal: reduce starvation-induced tail-latency for low-volume tenants without regressing 50th/95th latency for bulky multi-tenant workloads.

Why this variant?
- Continuous batching has been tuned around timeouts and urgency weights; intermittent starvation remains when low-rate requests sit behind long-lived KV cache sessions or when priority demotion interacts with probe traffic.
- Heartbeat: a tiny scheduler-triggered periodic flush (configurable interval + age threshold) aims to bound max wait-time for any request and provide a predictable worst-case latency while still allowing coalescing.

High-level hypothesis:
- A short heartbeat interval (2-10ms) will significantly reduce 99.9/99.99 tail for low-rate flows at cost of small throughput decrease and negligible median impact.
- There is a sweet spot interval where fairness improves but overall system throughput and large-batch kernel efficiency remain acceptable.

Experiment matrix (summary):
- workloads: small-concurrent (200 qps many short prompts), mixed-tenancy (10 heavy tenants + 200 low-rate tenants), bursty-probe (sudden 2x bursts), steady-high (baseline load used in canonical perf tests)
- heartbeat.interval_ms: 2, 5, 10, 25, 50, off
- max_coalesce_age_ms: 1, 5, 20 (used together with heartbeat to ensure we don't flush too early)
- demotion_shadow: true/false (whether demoted requests can be bumped at heartbeat)
- measurement windows: 15 minute stable run after warmup

Instrumentation notes:
- Enabled microtrace annotations at enqueue, pre-coalesce, post-coalesce, kernel-enter, kernel-exit, result-serialize.
- Added a lightweight counter for heartbeat-triggered flushes per queue and per-tenant.
- Collected kernel utilization, effective batch sizes, and token/sec.
- Exported per-request metadata: age_at_flush_ms, queued_batch_size, priority_tier.

Representative commands (local perf harness):
- ./harness --workload mixed-tenancy --rps 350 --seed 42 --run-for 900 --trace-level micro
- CONFIG_OVERRIDES='{"heartbeat_interval_ms":5,"max_coalesce_age_ms":5,"demotion_shadow":true}' ./serving_start.sh --env perf-local

Selected observations (raw):
- baseline (heartbeat=off): mixed-tenancy 99.99=1.42s, 99.9=430ms, 95=85ms, median=18ms. Effective batch size median=12, kernel occupancy 78%.
- h=2ms: 99.99=310ms, 99.9=210ms, 95=95ms, median=20ms. Effective batch size median=7, kernel occupancy 65%. Token/sec -8% vs baseline. Heartbeat flushes ~47k/min.
- h=5ms: 99.99=340ms, 99.9=240ms, 95=90ms, median=19ms. Effective batch size median=8, kernel occupancy 70%. Token/sec -5%. Heartbeat flushes ~21k/min.
- h=10ms: 99.99=560ms, 99.9=290ms, 95=86ms, median=18ms. Effective batch size median=10, kernel occupancy 75%. Token/sec -2%. Heartbeat flushes ~9k/min.
- h=25ms: tail moves toward baseline; negligible throughput impact.

Interpretation and tradeoffs:
- Very aggressive heartbeat (2ms) bounds extreme tail effectively but halves median batch size, reducing kernel throughput. This is useful for customers where tail SLA is strict for small-traffic tenants but harmful for pure high-throughput customers.
- 5-10ms is a pragmatic compromise: most of the tail improvement remains while keeping kernel efficiency within 70-75%.
- max_coalesce_age_ms interacts: when set to <= heartbeat interval, occasional premature flushes cost more. Best to set max_coalesce_age slightly > heartbeat interval to allow opportunistic coalescing until heartbeat hits.
- demotion_shadow=true: allowed demoted (low-priority) requests to be flushed when heartbeat hit; this improved fairness for low-rate tenants without causing priority inversion under tested mixes. We need more stress tests with adversarial demotion flows.

Artifacts and visualizations produced (links in linked_artifacts):
- per-tenant latency CDFs (median/95/99/99.9/99.99) for each interval setting.
- effective batch size distribution plots showing bimodality when heartbeat small.
- kernel occupancy heatmaps showing utilization drop at 2ms.

Edge cases & anomalies seen:
- When heartbeat=5ms and bursty probe traffic present, we saw periodic synchronization of probes causing 3x spike in heartbeat flushes every ~8s. Hypothesis: probe timing + heartbeat aligned causing microbursts. Mitigation: jitter heartbeat per-queue (random +/- 20%) reduces alignment.
- A small class of requests had age_at_flush > heartbeat_interval (observed at 2ms setting). Root cause traced to race in pre-coalesce snapshot where queue length measurement delayed by gc pause on trace agent. Added a local guard in codepath.

Performance regression checklist (for rollout to staging):
- Add telemetry: per-queue heartbeat rate, kernel batch-size histogram, kernel occupancy per-GPU.
- Implement per-tenant override: opt-out or opt-in heartbeat enforcement (customers with tight tail SLAs can enable for specific routes).
- Jitter heartbeat per-queue to avoid synchronization.
- Add experiment flag in runtime to enable demotion_shadow tests only when safe.

Open questions / next experiments:
- How does heartbeat interact with KV-cache-prefill latency? Do we flush too early preventing beneficial cache hits? Plan: trace cache-hit-rate per age bucket.
- Can we make heartbeat adaptive: stretch interval when batch growth rate high, shrink when queue age variance grows? Build a PID-ish controller prototype.
- Investigate a hybrid: heartbeat that only triggers when estimated batch-size falls below N for T ms (adaptive thresholding).

Action items (short-term):
- [Priya] implement jitter and guard for pre-coalesce snapshot races. Target: 2024-11-09.
- [Ethan] add per-tenant heartbeat telemetry and dashboard. Target: 2024-11-05.
- [Lena] run adversarial demotion shadow tests across 4 cluster configs and report regressions. Target: 2024-11-12.
- [Marco] prototype adaptive-heartbeat controller (simulator) and share results. Target: 2024-11-19.

Notes to self (informal):
- Need to compare token-cost delta per-100k tokens — rough estimate says 2-6% extra cost at 5ms. Show this to pricing/optimize team.
- Keep an eye on kernels that really care about batch shape (quantized kernels seem more forgiving than fp16).

Snippet: diagnostic microtrace (example)
- request id: r-0a1b2c3d
  enqueue_ts=1700000000100
  heartbeat_flush_ts=1700000000107
  age_at_flush_ms=7
  batch_size_at_flush=4
  kernel_enter_ts=1700000000110
  kernel_exit_ts=1700000000187
  total_latency_ms=87

Closing thought:
Heartbeat is a pragmatic, low-risk knob to trade predictable worst-case latency for a small throughput hit. We should treat it as another levers set in Optimize (per-route config + cost impact estimation). Next: validate across multi-node cluster with real traffic replay and coordinate with Optimize team for cost modeling.

-- end of diary entry --
